title: Executive Associate- [Open to Tier 0, 1 and 2 applicants]
description:
**Tiered Approach**

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

* **Tier 0:** UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
* **Tier 1:** Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
* **Tier 2:** UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
* **Tier 3 or no tier indicated:** All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

**Background**

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy.

The Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP’s Strategic Plan. BPPS’s staff provides technical advice to Country Offices; advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, South-South and Triangular cooperation initiatives, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its programme support efforts in close coordination and thematic synergy with the Crisis Bureau (CB).

The Front Office of BPPS is responsible for the smooth and seamless management of the substantive flow of information to and from BPPS, coordinating effective internal communications with BPPS teams, other Bureaus, the UNDP Executive Office, as well as communications with external partners. The Front Office plans and coordinates the BPPS Director and BPPS Deputy Director’s internal and external interactions and interventions based on priorities and agendas, in close collaboration with technical teams and other Bureaus as needed, ensuring the Director and Deputy Director’s successful provision of political leadership, strategic guidance, and managerial as well as programmatic priorities in full compliance with UNDP’s mandate.

With the opening of a new UNDP office in Madrid, where the BPPS Deputy Director and a number of BPPS teams will be relocating in the course of 2026, the Executive Associate will play a key role in supporting the establishment and smooth running of the new office, and its efficient interactions with the two other main BPPS locations (New York and Bonn).

**Position Purpose:**

Under the direct supervision of the BPPS Deputy Director and in coordination with their Special Assistant, the Executive Associate ensures that the Deputy Director receives the immediate administrative and operational support needed to execute their managerial functions. The incumbent works closely with both the Special Assistant and the Executive Associate of the Assistant Administrator and Director of BPPS, to strengthen coordination and complementarities in the Office of the Director and contribute toward the overall operations of the Front Office.

As one of the first points of contact with the Bureau for senior UNDP/UN staff and the full range of representatives of UNDP’s constituencies, the Executive Associate must deal with a heavy volume of requests and a wide range of highly sensitive matters under heavy time pressure.

Given the demands of protocol and interaction, often at high levels, the Executive Associate is required to perform the role with a calm demeanor under stressful circumstances, demonstrating efficiency and effectiveness in personal communication, knowledge of protocol, discretion and independent judgment, motivation and proactive attitude.

**The key functions of the Executive Associate are to ensure:**

* Effective and efficient functioning of the office of the Deputy Director of BPPS;
* Effective communications support to the office of the Deputy Director of BPPS;
* Support for effective relationship management by BPPS Directorate;
* Support the establishment and management of the new UNDP Office in Madrid

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

**1. Ensures effective and efficient functioning of the office of the Deputy Director, focusing on the achievement of the following results:**

* Coordination and maintenance of calendar of meetings and activities of the Deputy Director, including organizing meetings, confirming the Deputy Director’s participation in senior and high-level meetings and events, drafting replies to invitations and meetings and implementing protocol procedures;
* Management of the Deputy Director’s missions and representation schedule, including travel arrangements, communications with meeting organizers/country offices on logistics; itinerary, travel requests in Quantum, follow-up on authorization, clearances, visas, accommodation, and tickets necessary for travel;
* Ensuring compliance with respect to administrative procedures, rules, regulations and systems,;
* Use of automated office management systems for effective functioning of the Deputy Director’s office; maintenance of contact lists and rosters of high-level partners;
* Follow up on deadlines, commitments made, actions taken and coordination of collection and submission of the reports to the Deputy Director;
* Finance/accounts management support (i.e. processing payment requests, requisitions and claims pertaining to travels and retreats/ events) to the Deputy Director and Directorate;
* Support daily management of requests for reviews, approvals and clearances by the Deputy Director via email and DocuSign;
* Coverage and backstopping for the Executive Associate to the Director during peak times and absences

**2. Ensures effective communications support to the office of the Deputy Director of BPPS, focusing on achievement of the following results:**

* Effective monitoring and screening of correspondence arriving in and/or leaving the Deputy Director’s office. Review of incoming correspondence for the Deputy Director’s attention and prioritizing of documents according to action required; review, proofreading, and editing of all correspondence for proper clearance prior to the Deputy Director’s signature;
* Presentation of proposals to the Deputy Director and/or Special Assistant to streamline office procedures between the BPPS front office and other Headquarters units;
* Drafting and preparation of correspondence, directives, comments on behalf of the Deputy Director for their signature and ensuring follow-up as needed;; and
* Appropriate filing, including through automated filing systems, and ensuring safekeeping of confidential materials.
* Acts as secretary to meetings as requested by the Deputy Director, including drafting minutes, follow-ups, and reporting;
* Supports liaison with local counterparts in Spain, including the front offices of local/ federal Ministry officials and other UN agencies.

**3. Supports effective relationship management by BPPS front office, focusing on achievement of the following results:**

* Collaborate with the Special Assistant to the Deputy Director and broader BPPS front office in facilitating the Deputy Director’s interactions (in sensitive, political, diplomatic, and other instances) with various external partners of BPPS, such as ambassadors, donor country delegations, parliamentarians and high-level senior officials, as well as the Administrator and his office;
* Assist the Special Assistant to the Deputy Director in the research, obtaining and analysis of background materials for the preparation of presentations, talking points, briefings, meetings, official missions and appointments;
* Assist in the preparation of public information materials and folders, as requested;
* Support the organization of BPPS events such as townhalls, retreats or workshops, both at Headquarters and off-site; management of procurement of services, logistics, travel, visa, etc.
* Process the Deputy Director’s travel requests and post-travel functions in UNAll, in line with UNDP POPP, including calculation of DSA entitlements and claims and ensuring the timely settlement of claims.
* Process the Deputy Director’s travel fares in coordination with the local travel service (e.g. AMEX) in advance of missions.

**4. Supports the establishment and smooth running of the new UNDP office in Madrid, in collaboration with the BMS focal point in Madrid, focusing on achievement of the following results:**

* Office management, including coordinating with BMS for the necessary inventory of the Deputy Director’s office supplies and IT needs, and ensuring the readiness or usability of office/ meeting/ event spaces (e.g. good connection of video conferencing equipment for hybrid meetings);
* Orientation for BPPS colleagues relocating to Madrid in collaboration with the BMS focal point in Madrid, including advising on necessary local registrations (e.g. to obtain the TIE [foreign ID card]), support for obtainment of UN Grounds Pass, and office security registrations;
* Act as liaison with New York and Bonn BPPS offices in order to optimize the new configuration of BPPS across three main offices;
* Act as point of contact to prepare visits from UNDP leadership, including coordinating with Headquarters on the visit programme, facilitating the necessary travel documents for visas, support to secure UN Grounds Pass where needed, and liaising with counterparts/ Ministries in Spain on logistics and the needful security protocols.
* Acts as logistics coordinator for events involving the Madrid office staff and/or premises (e.g. preparation for official meetings or events hosted in the Madrid office, procurement of services or meeting supplies etc.).

**5. Facilitate knowledge building and management.**

* Provide sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.
* Organize specialized training as required.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: None

**Competencies**

* **Achieve Results:** LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline
* **Think Innovatively:** LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is a pragmatic problem solver, and makes improvements
* **Learn Continuously:** LEVEL 1: Open-minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback
* **Adapt with Agility:** LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible
* **Act with Determination:** LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in the face of adversity, confident
* **Engage and Partner:** LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships
* **Enable Diversity and Inclusion:** LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confronts discrimination

**Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies:**

* **Administration & Operations-Travel Policy and Procedures:** Knowledge of travel policy and procedures; ability to interpret travel policy, the Staff Rules, administrative circulars, and financial regulations and rules on travel-related matters.
* **Administration & Operations-Events management (including retreats, trainings & meetings):** Ability to manage events, including venue identification, accommodation, logistics, catering, transportation, and cash disbursements, etc.
* **Administration & Operations-UN Travel Documents:** Knowledge of the ERP regulatory frameworks and processes related to UN Travel and Expense Module Documents; ability to facilitate the issuance of UN travel documents for UNDP and provide help desk support to UNDP and other UN agencies; processing of visas, and ensuring oversight and endorsement
* **Administration & Operations-Off-boarding of personnel:** Knowledge of policy and procedures on administrative on- and off-boarding, including necessary clearance forms for returning office equipment, office ID, UNLP, cancellation of visa issued by host country, deletion of office email and Argus profile
* **Administration & Operations-Utilization of Corporate Credit Card:** Ability to ensure proper use of corporate credit card for official use; knowledge of relevant policy and procedures
* **Procurement -Procurement Management:** The ability to acquire goods, services or works from an outside external source
* **Business Direction & Strategy-Systems Thinking:** Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

**Required Skills and Experience**

**Education:**

* Secondary Education is required with specialized secretarial training.

OR

A University degree (bachelor’s degree) in Business or Public Administration, Economics, Political or Social Sciences will be given due consideration, but is not a requirement.

**Experience:**

* Minimum 7 years (with secondary education) or 4 years (with bachelor´s degree) of progressively responsible administrative or programme experience is required at the national and/or international level.
* Experience using IT software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and spreadsheet and database packages is required.
* Experience in handling web-based management and using ERP systems (i.e., Quantum) systems is required.
* Experience in logistics for workshops, travel arrangements, and office management is required.
* Experience conducting targeted research, analysis, and synthesis to support senior‑level decision‑making is desirable.
* Experience supporting senior leadership in a front office or similarly fast‑paced environment is desirable.
* Familiarity with the host country’s national administrative rules and processes, especially with regard to visas, travel, protocol, and other procedures that impact the Office of the Deputy Director, is an asset.
* Demonstrated experience in liaison, coordination, or maintaining professional relations with government officials, international organizations, NGOs, and/or external partners is highly desirable

**Language:**

* Fluency in English and Spanish is required.
* Working knowledge of other UN official languages is an asset.

**Equal opportunity**

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

**Probation**

For all new UNDP fixed-term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

**Right to select multiple candidates**

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

**Use of AI by candidates**

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

**Scam alert**

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert .

title: Power Systems Innovation Lead
description:
**Join Ferrovial: Where Innovation Meets Opportunity**
======================================================

Are you ready to elevate your career with a global leader in infrastructure solving complex problems and generating a positive outcome on people’s lives? At **Ferrovial** , we are not just a company; we are a community of innovators and trailblazers. Ferrovial is also leading the development of the New Terminal One at JFK International Airport. Ferrovial shares trade under the ticker symbol FER on two stock markets: Nasdaq in the U.S. (Nasdaq100 Index) and the Spanish Stock Exchanges (IBEX 35). Ferrovial is included in globally recognized sustainability indices such as the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Index. We operate in more than 15 countries and have a workforce of over 22,000 professionals worldwide. Ferrovial’s activity is carried out through our business units, including Highways, Airports, Construction, and Energy.

  

Our **Corporate** organization oversees business activities, providing strategic planning, communication, legal, finance and human resources services to the business units. As a member of our corporate organization, you will have a broad view of our company, further supporting your career development.

  

**Why Ferrovial?**

* **Global presence, local impact** : Be part of a company that is shaping the future of infrastructure worldwide, with challenging roles and projects that make a real difference.
* **Collaborative excellence** : Work alongside talented professionals in a collaborative environment where your ideas and contributions are valued.
* **Inclusive Culture:** Thrive in an innovative and respectful workplace that values every voice, celebrates what makes us unique and turns differences into innovation.
* **Career growth** : Benefit from global and cross-business unit mobility, with development processes designed to ensure your professional growth.
* **Compelling benefits and employee wellbeing** : Enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that rewards your hard work and dedication and take advantage of initiatives designed to support your physical and psychological health.
* **Productivity tools** : Utilize cutting-edge tools like Microsoft Copilot to enhance your productivity and efficiency.

  

**Job Description:**
====================

**About The Role**

  

*What if your next project didn't end up as a slide in a deck, but as technology actually running in an airport, a highway, a solar or wind power plant, or a data center?*

  

We are looking for a hands-on technical innovation leader who can work where energy strategy becomes real infrastructure: storage, grid connection, microgrids, electrification, critical power, resilience and renewable generation. You will assess emerging technologies with rigor, shape practical use cases and lead them through testing and validation, building the evidence the business needs to decide whether to invest, scale or stop.

  

You will join Corporate Innovation and work across Ferrovial’s businesses: Airports, Cintra, Ferrovial Energy and Digital Infrastructure. Success in the role requires strong engineering judgement, the ability to distinguish genuine breakthroughs from incremental improvements, and the credibility to engage technical and business stakeholders alike—translating complex challenges into well-structured pilots, clear investment decisions and scalable business opportunities.

  

This is a unique opportunity to influence the future of infrastructure by bringing cutting-edge technologies from concept to real-world deployment across a global leader in the sector. Experience in mission-critical environments, including data centers, is a plus, but not essential.

  

**Key Responsibilitie** s

* Lead energy, sustainability and resilience projects from technology identification through pilot, business case and scale-up recommendation
* Design and run proofs of concept with business units, OEMs, engineering partners, research centers and startups — setting your own KPIs and decision gates
* Bring real engineering judgment to grid connection, electrification, storage, microgrids, critical power, energy management and renewable generation infrastructure (solar and wind plants)
* Translate complex technical options and uncertainty into clear business cases for senior leadership
* Explore emerging low-carbon technologies — carbon capture and utilization, green molecules, hydrogen, e-fuels, biogenic routes — and assess their real potential
Optionally contribute to projects on low-carbon materials, embodied carbon and circularity  

  

**Qualification** s

* Hold an engineering or equivalent technical degree, ideally in electrical, energy, mechanical, industrial, civil or building-services engineering
* 8–12 years of experience in corporate innovation, technical office roles, or critical asset operations (energy, renewables, infrastructure, data centers)
* Real engineering judgment, not just strategic vision — you can defend a technical decision, not just frame one
* Relevant knowledge of energy and infrastructure systems—including grid connection, electrification, efficiency, storage, microgrids, controls, critical power or energy management—and how they interact with thermal, water and resilience requirements
* Familiarity with low-carbon materials, carbon technologies, embodied carbon, circularity and lifecycle value, with sound judgement on when to involve Ferrovial’s specialist teams
* Ability to build effective relationships across business units and with operators, OEMs, engineering partners, startups, universities and investors, acting as a connector rather than an operational owner
* Ability to move across asset classes: what you learn on a wind farm should be useful on an airport, a highway or a data center
* A drive to see things through: you don't stop at validation — you want to see the technology scale
* Comfort working with uncertainty and with very different stakeholders — from an OEM engineer to a business director

We are not looking for a purely strategic profile without hands-on engineering. Someone who prefers staying in day-to-day operations rather than pushing change forward. Someone who wants to specialize in a single asset class.

**Seize the challenge. Move the world together!** Innovative, creative, respectful, and diverse are some of the ways we describe ourselves. We are motivated by challenges, and we collaborate across our business units to move the world together. Your journey to a fulfilling career starts here!

Ferrovial is an equal opportunity employer. We treat all jobs applications equally, regardless of gender, color, race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, covered veteran status or protected genetic information (each, a “Protected Class”), or any other protected class in accordance with applicable laws.

description:
### **Position**

**Being part of LOEWE** gives you the opportunity of learning new things every day and working with people passionate about what they do, in a fast moving and ambitious company.

Join our Visual Merchandising team in this **temporary opportunity** and support the creation of inspiring retail experiences across our stores and windows. Reporting to the VM Manager, you will play a key role in bringing LOEWE’s visual identity to life, supporting seasonal launches, events, and VM guideline development.

### **Job responsibilities**

**Your role will be:**

* Support the VM Manager in the development and execution of Leather Goods (LG) visual merchandising, including accessory styling and window styling guideline shoots.
* Coordinate samples, props, and product organization throughout the VM guideline creation process for the LG category.
* Assist in the development and production of visual merchandising guidelines for LG across stores.
* Support the implementation of LG seasonal window displays, in-store launches, pop-ins, pop-ups, and special events.
* Ensure visual merchandising materials and assets related to LG are organized and updated.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to help deliver LG projects on time and according to LOEWE’s brand standards.
* Monitor details across all VM projects to ensure consistency and excellence in execution.
* Provide day-to-day administrative and operational support to the Visual Merchandising team.
* Adapt quickly to changing priorities and business needs while maintaining a proactive and solution-oriented mindset.

### **Profile**

**What is important for the role:**

* 1+ year of experience in Visual Merchandising, Retail, or Fashion.
* Strong interest in Leather Goods, fashion, arts, crafts, and design, with a good aesthetic sensibility.
* Excellent attention to detail and strong organizational and time management skills.
* Proactive, flexible, and solutions-oriented, with a collaborative mindset.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, InDesign, Illustrator).
* Fluent English; Spanish is a plus.

### **Additional information**

**About us:**

Founded in Spain in 1846, LOEWE is the second-oldest luxury fashion house in the world. Since 2025, the House is under the creative direction of Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez, guided by a rich artistic sensibility and an imaginative exploration of craft. This new chapter builds on core sensibilities of LOEWE: an intellectual and playful approach to fashion, the vibrant spirit of Spanish lifestyle, and unmatched leather expertise.

At LOEWE we are committed to a culture that welcomes all, regardless of gender, ethnicity, socioeconomic background and abilities, including people with disabilities of all types. Our aim is for everyone to feel valued, included, and empowered to contribute their best.

If you think this role is made for you, please send us your CV!

***LOEWE*** 
**MAISON**
-----------------------

Steeped in art and historical references, rooted in craft and tradition, Loewe has been reinventing leather craftmanship for almost 200 years. From its birth in Madrid in 1846 to its latest collection dedicated to the elegance of Chinese monochrome ceramics, the Maison’s journey has been defined by its core values: energy, creativity, and a thoroughly modern approach blended with traditional techniques.
  
Craft at Loewe is unconditionally bound up with art, an endless source of inspiration: from the British Arts & Craft masters to the whimsical world of Studio Ghibli, art is at the heart of every collection – and the House is committed to supporting the artists and creators informing its work.
  
Today, Loewe’s master artisans combine their craft knowledge, accumulated over generations, with new technologies to produce iconic objects presenting both instant appeal and enduring style: true incarnations of Loewe’s ideals and vision.
  
Radical and ever-evolving: here’s to another 200 years of Loewe history
  
Since 2013, Jonathan Anderson, Loewe’s Creative Director, has been carrying this vision ever further. One of the leading designers of his generation, Anderson has spearheaded a major rejuvenation of the House.
  
Through a redesign of the brand identity, a modern articulation of its commitment to craft (with the launch of the Loewe Foundation Craft Prize, for instance), and a series of critically acclaimed and genre-defining Women’s and Men’s collections, Loewe has been further elevated as an influential and global cultural force.
  
At the intersection of fashion, craft and culture, Loewe’s ambition is to be radical and ever-evolving. Craft and luxury are inextricably linked, and at Loewe, the one makes the other feel more accessible and tangible. By showing how the collections are made and honouring the complex artisanal processes behind them, it becomes possible to see their value and their merit. And by adding a cultural dimension – involving fine arts, film, dance, etc. –, Loewe has become a vibrant force for creativity and innovation, ensuring the brand’s durability for another 200 years… and more.

title: Senior CRM Lifecycle + Journeys Manager
description:
**ABOUT QUINCE**

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world's finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

**OUR CULTURE**

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren't interested in replicating how others do retail. We're building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that's been done before.

* We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
* Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
* Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you're someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

**THE ROLE**

The **Senior Manager, CRM Lifecycle + Journeys** owns every triggered flow in the customer journey across email, SMS, push, and in-app for UK, Germany, and France. You will build the automation engine that runs Quince's retention programme: from the welcome series a UK customer sees the day we launch, to the win-back flow that recovers a French customer six months later.

This is a builder role. You will spend most of your first six months in Iterable and the CDP. You will write the flow logic, set up the data pipes, design the experiments, and ship the AI agents that take work out of building, testing, and reporting on flows. The Director, CRM owns the retention strategy and the campaign calendar. You own the triggered flow programme that runs alongside it.

Two constraints shape this job. UK and EU privacy rules mean the US lifecycle playbook does not transfer unchanged: you will rebuild the identity-resolution layer and shift weight toward logged-in and app behaviour. Channel economics also differ across markets, with SMS in particular materially more expensive in Europe than in the US, so the sequencing of email, SMS, push, and in-app per flow per market is not the same as the US default.

You will be joining a team that values speed, candor, and rigour. This role is for you if you like building things, you can hold a roadmap in one hand and a SQL query in the other, and you have an opinion on how AI changes lifecycle work over the next 18 months.

**Responsibilities**

* Build, launch, and own every triggered lifecycle flow for UK (July 2026), DE (October 2026), and FR (November 2026): welcome, browse abandon, cart abandon, post-purchase, low stock, back in stock, win-back, replenishment, care instructions.
* Partner with MarTech to Ship AI agents and tooling that take work out of flow build, copy, segmentation, and QA. Target at least one end-to-end CRM agent in production by EoY1 and a 50% reduction in flow concept-to-deployment time within 90 days.
* Partner with the Data team to run the triggered-flow testing roadmap with statistically sound design. Minimum 6 A/B tests per quarter per flow per market.
* Build channel-cost decision logic across email, SMS, push, and in-app per flow per market.
* Recover signal lost from fingerprinting and consent restrictions in UK/EU by pushing app and logged-in routing for non-consenting users.
* Stand up and run the localisation pipeline with freelance copywriters for EN-UK, DE, and FR. Localised flow content live before each market launch.
* Partner with tech team to maintain CDP quality across UK/EU: data model, integrations (Iterable, Attentive, app SDK, site events), data hygiene, latency, and identity-resolution accuracy.

**Qualifications**

**Required:**

* 6+ years lifecycle/CRM marketing in DTC or ecommerce, including at least 3 years owning automated/triggered flows end to end (not campaign/blast).
* Hands-on with Iterable (preferred), or comparable ESP (Braze, Klaviyo, SFMC). Must have built flows in the tool, not just briefed them.
* Hands-on with a CDP: Segment, mParticle, Hightouch, Census, or similar. Must understand identity resolution and data hygiene.
* Has built or deployed AI agents or LLM workflows in a marketing context (copy, segmentation, flow logic, QA). If you have not shipped one yet, you can describe the one you would ship in your first 90 days here.
* SQL proficient. Can self-serve in Looker, Lookr, or BigQuery without waiting for an analyst.
* A/B testing rigour. Knows what statistical significance means and where it breaks in lifecycle (sample size, primary metric selection, novelty effects).
* Working knowledge of UK/EU privacy law (GDPR, PECR) and consent management. Understands what changes operationally when fingerprinting is restricted.
* Detail-oriented. Triggered flows live or die on edge cases (locale, currency, time zone, opt-in state, suppression rules).
* Strong cross-functional operator. Will work daily with creative, brand, data science, tech, and US CRM counterparts.

**Preferred:**

* Multi-market lifecycle experience (UK + DE or FR), fashion or home goods background, app-native lifecycle experience, fluency in DE or FR.

**WHY QUINCE?**

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY**

Quince provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applications for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran or military status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Quince is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to complete your application or to perform the essential functions of a role at Quince, please let us know by completing this accommodation form. We review all requests individually and will work with you to determine appropriate accommodations on a case-by-case basis.

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check. Quince will conduct background checks in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

*Security Advisory: Beware of Frauds*

At Quince, we're dedicated to recruiting top talent who share our drive for innovation. To safeguard candidates, Quince emphasizes legitimate recruitment practices. Initial communication is primarily via official Quince email addresses and LinkedIn; beware of deviations. Personal data and sensitive information will not be solicited during the application phase. This new chapter builds on core sensibilities of LOEWE: an intellectual and playful approach to fashion, the vibrant spirit of Spanish lifestyle, and unmatched leather expertise.

At LOEWE we are committed to a culture that welcomes all, regardless of gender, ethnicity, socioeconomic background and abilities, including people with disabilities of all types. Our aim is for everyone to feel valued, included, and empowered to contribute their best.

***LOEWE*** 
**MAISON**
-----------------------

Steeped in art and historical references, rooted in craft and tradition, Loewe has been reinventing leather craftmanship for almost 200 years. From its birth in Madrid in 1846 to its latest collection dedicated to the elegance of Chinese monochrome ceramics, the Maison’s journey has been defined by its core values: energy, creativity, and a thoroughly modern approach blended with traditional techniques.
  
Craft at Loewe is unconditionally bound up with art, an endless source of inspiration: from the British Arts & Craft masters to the whimsical world of Studio Ghibli, art is at the heart of every collection – and the House is committed to supporting the artists and creators informing its work.
  
Today, Loewe’s master artisans combine their craft knowledge, accumulated over generations, with new technologies to produce iconic objects presenting both instant appeal and enduring style: true incarnations of Loewe’s ideals and vision.
  
Radical and ever-evolving: here’s to another 200 years of Loewe history
  
Since 2013, Jonathan Anderson, Loewe’s Creative Director, has been carrying this vision ever further. One of the leading designers of his generation, Anderson has spearheaded a major rejuvenation of the House.
  
Through a redesign of the brand identity, a modern articulation of its commitment to craft (with the launch of the Loewe Foundation Craft Prize, for instance), and a series of critically acclaimed and genre-defining Women’s and Men’s collections, Loewe has been further elevated as an influential and global cultural force.
  
At the intersection of fashion, craft and culture, Loewe’s ambition is to be radical and ever-evolving. Craft and luxury are inextricably linked, and at Loewe, the one makes the other feel more accessible and tangible. By showing how the collections are made and honouring the complex artisanal processes behind them, it becomes possible to see their value and their merit. And by adding a cultural dimension – involving fine arts, film, dance, etc. –, Loewe has become a vibrant force for creativity and innovation, ensuring the brand’s durability for another 200 years… and more.

Wood Mackenzie is the global leader in analytics, insights and proprietary data across the entire energy and natural resources landscape.

For over 50 years our work has guided the decisions of the world’s most influential energy producers, utilities companies, financial institutions and governments.

Now, with the world’s energy system more complex and interconnected than ever before, sector-specific views are no longer enough. That’s why we’ve redefined what’s possible with Intelligence Connected.

By fusing our unparalleled proprietary data with the sharpest analytical minds, all supercharged by Synoptic AI, we deliver a clear, interconnected view of the entire value chain. Our trusted team of 2,700 experts across 30 countries breaks siloes and connects industries, markets and regions across the globe.

This empowers our customers to identify risk sooner, spot opportunities faster and recalibrate strategy with confidence – whether planning days, weeks, months or decades ahead.

Wood Mackenzie  
Intelligence Connected

**WoodMac.com**

**Wood Mackenzie Brand Video**

**Wood Mackenzie Values**

* Inclusive – we succeed together
* Trusting – we choose to trust each other
* Customer committed – we put customers at the heart of our decisions
* Future Focused – we accelerate change
* Curious – we turn knowledge into action

The Vice President, Head of EMEA Power and Renewables Research will lead Wood Mackenzie's Power and Renewables Research team for the EMEA region. The role combines team leadership, development of the research roadmap, commercial ownership of the Lens EMEA Power and Renewables offering, senior level industry engagement and collaboration with internal stakeholders (product, sales, marketing, consulting) to drive impact and commercial success.

The candidate will define and deliver the research roadmap for the EMEA Power and Renewables offering, lead the team responsible for shaping Wood Mackenzie's EMEA power and renewables market intelligence, and represent Wood Mackenzie across the region's energy industry through frequent engagement with clients, media and industry stakeholders. They will work closely with colleagues across research, product, sales, marketing and consulting to ensure our market views and product offering remain relevant, differentiated, timely, actionable and commercially successful.

As Wood Mackenzie continues to evolve from a leading research provider into a connected intelligence platform, spanning data, analytics, technology and expert insight, this role will strengthen and extend our leadership in EMEA power and renewables markets.

**Key responsibilities**

* Own the research content strategy for EMEA power and renewables and decide how the offering develops in response to market changes and client demand, while providing predictive and actionable intelligence. Ensure that the EMEA Power and Renewables views feed into Wood Mackenzie’s broader integrated and connected offerings across its portfolio.

* Lead, coach and develop a team of research analysts and senior analysts covering wind, solar, energy storage and power markets across EMEA, building analytical depth, subject matter expertise, and succession plans within the team.

* Hold commercial management responsibility for the EMEA Power and Renewables Lens offering, tracking performance and working with product, sales and marketing to ensure the offering meets its commercial targets.

* Define and deliver the roadmap for EMEA Power and Renewables, working with the product team to prioritise new content, data, and functionality that meet evolving client needs.

* Partner closely with sales, marketing and consulting teams to support renewals, upsell and bespoke client engagements, and to effectively market the team's research and the wider Lens offering.

* Produce and oversee high-quality, forward-looking thought leadership, including written research, commentary, and presentations, that anticipate and respond to major developments across wind, solar, storage and power markets.

* Represent Wood Mackenzie through frequent engagement with the industry — media, conferences and client events — building a distinctive and authoritative public profile that reinforces our position as the most trusted and integrated source of EMEA power and renewables intelligence.

* Build and sustain relationships with senior clients and prospects, including industry C-suite, investment leadership, and government and institutional stakeholders, driving commercial outcomes and deepening Wood Mackenzie's market influence across the region.

* Own headcount planning, hiring and resource allocation for the team, ensuring the right mix of skills and coverage across the region's markets.

**Experience**

You will bring 10+ years of experience in power and renewables market research, analysis or consulting, potentially gained within a major energy company, utility, developer, or a leading research and analytics firm.

You will have:

* Expertise in EMEA power market fundamentals, complemented by strong working knowledge of wind, solar and energy storage markets.

* Demonstrated experience leading and developing a team of analysts or researchers, including hiring, coaching and performance management.

* Commercial experience managing a subscription, portfolio, research or data product, including ownership of a product roadmap and working cross-functionally with sales, product and marketing to drive commercial performance.

* Strong written skills and a proven track record of delivering market analysis to inform high-stakes strategic, investment, or policy decisions.

* Experience representing an organization's views externally — through media commentary, conference speaking, published research, and client presentations. Recognised as a subject matter expert or thought leader.
* Established relationships with senior figures across the EMEA energy sector, including executives, investors, and government or institutional stakeholders.

* Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to distil complex market dynamics into compelling narratives for senior audiences.

* Familiarity with data-driven and quantitative approaches to market analysis, and an appetite to work at the frontier of how power and renewables market intelligence is developed.

* Strong problem-solving skills and AI-forward thinking

**Equal Opportunities**

We are an equal opportunities employer. Education Centre Director
description:
About Boundless Life

Boundless Life is redefining the way families live, work, and learn by empowering them to embrace a nomadic lifestyle that fosters deeper connections and personal growth. We provide family-friendly accommodations, an innovative education system that travels with you, and vibrant communities of like-minded individuals.

Since our founding in 2021, we’ve rapidly expanded to eight locations across Europe, Asia, and Latin America, bringing together over 200 team members from diverse backgrounds. Our growth reflects our commitment to transforming the experience economy and making a meaningful impact on how families integrate work, education, and exploration into their lives.

At Boundless Life, we believe in the power of community and the importance of a holistic approach to education. Our programs are designed to inspire curiosity, build resilience, and nurture a global perspective. We combine a project-based, place-based learning with the freedom to live and learn anywhere, for families who want more than a traditional school can offer. Our Education Centres are the heart of everything we do.

Role Overview

Estepona is one of our most established and beloved locations — a flagship of what the Boundless model is. The Education Centre Director who joins here will inherit something that is already working and will be responsible for taking it further.

This is a role for a leader who can come into an existing team, earn trust quickly, raise the bar through coaching and consistency, and build on strong foundations without disrupting what is already good. You are not here to reinvent. You are here to lead, deepen, and improve.

As Education Centre Director, you are the educational leader of the location. You are responsible for how the learning happens and how it is brought to life by your team. You know your educators deeply, coach them continuously, hold high standards, and ensure every cohort delivers on the Boundless promise.You will report directly to the General Manager, with a dotted reporting line to the Head of Education Excellence.

This structure allows you to focus primarily on pedagogical leadership, instructional coaching, and developing your educator team, while the General Manager owns the broader location operations. The role demands someone who is energised by that scale, not overwhelmed by it.

What You'll Do

*Educator Leadership and Team Development*

* Lead, coach, and manage an established team of educators through structured 1:1s, regular classroom observations, and direct, specific feedback
* Set clear expectations for performance and conduct from day one, address gaps independently, and build individual development plans for every member of the team
* Hold a high bar consistently — this means celebrating what is working and naming what is not, without waiting for a formal review cycle
* Build and maintain a team culture that is engaged and resilient through an intense cohort calendar and a demanding daily schedule
* Contribute to hiring decisions alongside the Head of Education Excellence when the team expands or changes

*Curriculum Execution and Educational Quality*

* Ensure the Boundless curriculum is implemented consistently and with fidelity to our global methodology and standards — you do not design the curriculum, you make sure it comes to life as intended
* Ensure project-based and place-based learning happen on the ground, incorporating the extraordinary context of the location meaningfully and in alignment with global curriculum standards
* Observe classes regularly and give educators specific, actionable feedback that leads to real change
* Surface implementation challenges to the global education team and bring solutions alongside them

*Family Relationships*

* Serve as a trusted, visible presence for families — including those who are returning to Boundless and have high expectations of the experience
* Handle family concerns and escalations independently and with confidence, without unnecessary escalation to global leadership
* Contribute to a strong admissions and intake experience that sets every cohort up well

*Running the Education Centre*

* Lead the essential day-to-day running of the Education Centre in close partnership with the General Manager and central teams.
* Own educator administration, family communication, safeguarding, and the smooth delivery of ECAs and field trips.
* Support local partners, systems and practical centre needs where required, while keeping educational leadership and people development as the priority.
* You will be involved in the Boundless Summer Camp cohorts, maintaining the same standards of team leadership and family experience.

Role Requirements

* 85% or more of educators and facilitators in the centre meet or exceed their role-specific impact metrics

Who You'll Work With

That is not a small thing to be part of.

You will also benefit from:

* A global community of educators, families, and team members who care deeply about what they are building
* Real ownership of your location and your team's development
* The chance to grow as the organisation grows — this role has significant room to evolve

Our diverse portfolio of ecosystems and operating companies gives us the scale and complexity to master every SEO specialization—from technical infrastructure and content architecture, to AI search optimization, local market dominance, and brand authority building. By partnering with world-class Product, Engineering, Data and Marketing teams, we leverage cutting-edge tools and data-driven insights to deliver exceptional performance and measurable impact across major search engines and dynamic digital ecosystems.

title: Video Producer
description:
**About Frontiers**

At Frontiers, our purpose is simple yet ambitious: to make science open. We believe open science empowers the global scientific community to accelerate discovery and develop the solutions needed for healthy lives on a healthy planet.

We are one of the world’s largest and most influential open-access research publishers. Every article we publish is peer-reviewed and quality-certified, ensuring research is accessible to everyone, everywhere. To date, Frontiers research has been viewed over 4 billion times, demonstrating the real-world impact of science without barriers.

Joining Frontiers means being part of a global, mission-driven organization at the intersection of science, technology, and innovation — working alongside passionate colleagues who care deeply about advancing knowledge for the benefit of society. To learn more about our impact and culture, please watch this video.

**About the role**

We're looking for a **Video Producer** to join our Visual Design team and work closely with the Senior Video Producer to expand and accelerate Frontiers' video storytelling. In this role, you'll take ownership of video productions from planning and filming through to post-production, creating interviews, talking-head content, b-roll, and studio shoots for company-wide communications and campaigns.

As a second videographer, you'll have the opportunity to lead independent shoots while also supporting larger productions led by the Senior Video Producer. You'll combine strong technical video skills with excellent organization, ensuring that shoots run smoothly, footage meets Frontiers' creative and technical standards, and media assets are efficiently managed throughout the production process.

You'll work closely with colleagues across Communications and Visual Design, as well as researchers, authors, employees, external contributors, and production partners. If you enjoy working both behind the camera and behind the scenes, solving problems on the go, and creating high-quality visual content in a fast-paced environment, you'll thrive in this role.

You'll also contribute to improving video production workflows by using technology, AI-powered tools, and consistent production practices to streamline scheduling, media management, transcription, subtitling, and post-production.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Coordinate video shoots end-to-end, including scheduling interviews, talking-head sessions, b-roll, and studio productions with internal and external stakeholders.
* Prepare and distribute call sheets, coordinate shoot logistics, and ensure crews and on-camera participants have clear information about locations, timings, requirements, and expectations.
* Scout and book filming locations, studios, and meeting spaces, coordinating travel arrangements and equipment transportation for shoots outside Lausanne.
* Prepare, test, organize, and maintain camera, lighting, audio, and studio equipment, ensuring all production kits are ready for each assignment.
* Independently film interviews, talking-heads, b-roll, and studio content, operating professional camera, lighting, and audio equipment to a consistently high standard.
* Work as a second camera operator and provide technical support on larger and multi-camera productions led by the Senior Video Producer.
* Welcome and brief on-camera participants, helping guests feel comfortable and confident throughout the filming process while ensuring required release forms and consent documentation are completed.
* Ingest, back up, organize, and archive raw footage following established folder structures, file-naming conventions, and media management practices.
* Support post-production by cutting and editing footage, applying colour grading and established brand guidelines, creating and using motion graphics, and preparing subtitles and AI-assisted transcriptions.
* Work with Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, and other relevant production tools to support high-quality video delivery.
* Collaborate with internal teams and external production partners, including freelance crew, studios, equipment suppliers, editors, and post-production specialists.
* Identify and resolve technical, logistical, and production challenges independently while maintaining quality, schedules, and production standards.
* Contribute to improving video production workflows, playbooks, and best practices, helping the team increase production capacity and deliver content efficiently.

  
**Requirements**  

* 2–3 years of hands-on experience in video production, videography, or a similar role, with experience taking video projects from production planning and filming through to post-production.
* Strong technical video production skills, including professional camera operation, lighting, and audio recording, with the ability to independently deliver high-quality footage.
* A strong portfolio or showreel demonstrating relevant camera, lighting, sound, editing, and/or studio production experience.
* Proficiency in video editing and post-production tools, particularly Adobe Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve, with experience in editing, colour grading, and Adobe After Effects/motion graphics.
* Strong production coordination and organizational skills, with experience managing shoot schedules, call sheets, locations, equipment, travel, production documentation, and digital media organization, including footage ingestion, file naming, folder structures, and backups.
* Experience with Microsoft 365 and project collaboration tools such as Jira, Confluence, or similar platforms.
* Fluency in English, with strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively with internal teams, external production partners, and on-camera participants.
* A proactive and solutions-oriented approach, with the ability to troubleshoot technical and logistical challenges calmly and independently while maintaining production and brand standards.
* Familiarity with AI-powered tools for transcription, subtitling, or production workflows is an advantage.
* Willingness and ability to travel for filming assignments and flexibility to accommodate changing production schedules.
* A bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification in Media Production, Film, Communications, or a related field is preferred, although relevant practical experience will also be considered.
* Experience in corporate communications, science communication, or event filming is an advantage.

  
**Benefits**  

* We prioritise office presence and emphasise in-person collaboration, but also offer appropriate adjustments where needed, in line with company policy
* Extra wellbeing days on top of your annual leave allowance
* Up to 3 paid volunteering days each year
* 24/7 confidential Employee Assistance Programme (wellbeing, mental health, legal & financial support)
* Learning & development support via the Frontiers Learning Hub

***Equal opportunity statement***

***Frontiers actively embraces diversity and is a safe and welcoming workplace. Recruitment is free from discrimination – including based on race, national or ethnic origin, age, religion, disability, sex, gender identity or sexual orientation. With employees from more than 50 different nations, our diversity creates vibrant teams and constantly challenges us to appreciate multiple perspectives.***

**Who We Are**  
Marketbridge partners with leading B2B brands to create unified Go-to-Market® systems that connect strategy, AI, creativity, activation and measurement. With a team of 350+ across North America and Europe, Marketbridge supports clients worldwide, ranging from Fortune 1000 enterprises to venture-backed, high-growth companies across technology, financial services, healthcare, industrial and consumer sectors. Marketbridge is seeking a Director, Media Strategy to lead the development and execution of integrated media strategies for enterprise B2B clients. Working alongside a team of talented media professionals, and leading the charge on strategy media strategies with cross-functional partners, you will help build best-in-class, brand-to-demand campaigns that deliver measurable business results.

**What You’ll Be Doing**

The Director, Media Strategy will be responsible for developing and overseeing B2B media strategies across a portfolio of client accounts. This role requires a strong understanding of B2B media channels, vendors, platforms, and emerging trends, along with the ability to translate client objectives into actionable media plans.

You will serve as a strategic media lead for clients, guide planning and activation teams, and collaborate closely with account management, demand strategy, creative, analytics, and channel specialists to deliver integrated and effective campaigns.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Media Strategy and Planning**

* Develop comprehensive B2B media strategies that align with client marketing objectives, target audiences, and business goals
* Translate broader marketing and demand-generation strategies into actionable, full-funnel media plans
* Identify and evaluate media opportunities across programmatic, paid social, SEM, trade publications, outdoor, traditional media, and other relevant channels
* Provide strategic direction throughout campaign planning, activation, optimization, and reporting

* Build a strong understanding of each client’s business, industry, audiences, and competitive landscape

* Experience leading client presentations and providing strategic media recommendations
* Previous experience mentoring, managing, or providing direction to media professionals
* Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship-management skills
* Ability to manage multiple client accounts and quickly shifting priorities in a fast-paced agency environment
